answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 16 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the juniper solution is checked at the garden gate and logged, the velvet audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 37 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
